page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Laosv4 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and includes 2880 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. However, memory bandwidth is a notable tradeoff, with read-only small block and large block bandwidth tests registering in the bottom 25%. Database operations and software compilation tasks also show weaker performance, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput maintain average tiers.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial 2880 GB local storage, the L4aos_v4 offers a resource-dense profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extreme memory bandwidth. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high local storage capacity alongside moderate compute power. Appropriate workloads include memory-bound caching layers, moderate database operations, text processing, and light web serving.
